identity.name: KRN HEAT EXCHANGE N REF L

summary.oneLiner: KRN Heat is transitioning from a pure-play fin-and-tube supplier to an integrated thermal solutions provider, driven by a newly commissioned 6x capacity facility and high-growth segments like Data Centers and Bus AC. While Q4FY26 showed strong top-line growth (Consolidated Revenue +33.5% YoY), inventory buildup due to export logistics and new product ramp-up temporarily suppressed cash flows, setting the stage for significant operating leverage in FY27 as utilization targets 50%.

one-line thesis: KRN Heat is transitioning from a pure-play fin-and-tube supplier to an integrated thermal solutions provider, driven by a newly commissioned 6x capacity facility and high-growth segments like Data Centers and Bus AC. While Q4FY26 showed strong top-line growth (Consolidated Revenue +33.5% YoY), inventory buildup due to export logistics and new product ramp-up temporarily suppressed cash flows, setting the stage for significant operating leverage in FY27 as utilization targets 50%.
financial scorecard: Consolidated Revenue Rs.181.4cr (+33.5% YoY); EBITDA Rs.33.55cr (+77.6% YoY, ~18.5% margin); PAT Rs.23.36cr (+57.1% YoY). Standalone Revenue Rs.204.9cr (+55% YoY). One-offs: Inventory spike due to Rs.120cr UAE order dispatch delay (geopolitical/freight) and Rs.8cr unbilled exports; BIS regulation stockpiling.
guidance: FY27 New Facility Utilization: 50% (Targeting 80% in FY28); Export Revenue: ~2x YoY (from Rs.100cr); Bus AC Revenue Target: Rs.150cr (15% market share); Data Center Revenue Share: ~19% in FY27 (up from 16%); Margins: Expected expansion via PLI (5%), RIFS (1.56% of top-line), and solar savings.
order book & pipeline: Export order book ~Rs.120cr (includes Data Center); Bus AC secured 2-3 OEMs with regular supply; Data Center orders have 6-7 month lead times; Rolling orders from domestic HVAC majors.
segment / subsidiary detail: Data Center: 16% of FY26 revenue, targeting 19% in FY27; key clients Schneider Electric, Vertiv (approval complete). Bus AC: Rs.10cr in FY26, targeting Rs.150cr. New Products: WOT, Roll-bond, Bar & Plate (Railways approved for trial), Dry Air Coolers. Exports: US, Europe, UAE.
growth verticals / optionality: Railway AC systems (6-8 month approval timeline); Liquid Cooling (CDU/Plate heat exchangers) for AI Data Centers (R&D ongoing, launch expected next year); Micro-channel heat exchangers (MCHX) portfolio addition by year-end.
margins & cost dynamics: Raw material pass-through: 100% of Copper/Aluminum LME and USD-INR fluctuations passed on quarterly. Margin drivers: PLI incentive (5%), RIFS state incentive (1.56% of revenue for 10 years), solar power savings. Headwinds: High depreciation and overheads from new facility ramp-up.
capex / expansion: Major capacity expansion (6x) complete. Minor incremental capex of Rs.30-40cr planned over next 2 years for line balancing and geometry adjustments for Data Center specific products.
capital allocation: Board approved QIP up to Rs.500cr (primarily for working capital to support rapid growth and inventory needs); final size and utilization under review. Dividend policy not explicitly detailed but focus on reinvestment for growth.
risks & watch-items: Working Capital Strain: Inventory days elevated to ~2.5 months due to logistics delays and new product stocking. Regulatory: BIS certification delays for inner groove tubes impacting imports. Geopolitical: Freight cost volatility and dispatch delays to UAE. Execution: Ramp-up speed of 8 new product lines.
management quality / tone: Highly confident on long-term structural growth (Data Center, Bus AC); transparent about short-term working capital inefficiencies; aggressive on market share capture (15% in Bus AC); cautious on precise near-term numbers due to ramp-up variables.
non-obvious takeaways: The inventory buildup is largely strategic (BIS hedging) and logistical (UAE dispatch delay) rather than demand weakness; Rs.8cr of March exports are already shipped but unbilled, artificially inflating inventory and depressing Q4 revenue recognition. The company is effectively a 'hidden' liquid cooling play via its development of plate heat exchangers for CDUs.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Need for efficient thermal management in AI-driven data centers | KRN Heat Exchanger | beneficiary | High | Direct supplier to Schneider/Vertiv; expanding into liquid cooling components; 19% revenue share target. |
| Transition to electric buses and need for localized AC systems | KRN Heat Exchanger | beneficiary | High | High backward integration; targeting 15% market share; Rs.150cr revenue target. |
| Supply chain diversification away from China | KRN Heat Exchanger | beneficiary | Med | Exports doubling; competing with European/US suppliers rather than Chinese mass producers. |

themes.title: Data-Center & AI electrical/cooling buildout
themes.need: AI/data-center capex pulls transformers, switchgear, gensets, HVAC/cooling, optical and cabling AND a new high-margin cooling supply chain. CUMMINSIND flags DC at ~30-35% of domestic powergen with a demand surge since Oct-2025; VENUSPIPES won a ~INR185cr DC-cooling LOI; AEROFLEX building liquid-cooling skids; BLUESTARCO on DC MEP; STLTECH/NETWEB on optical + HPC/AI servers (STLTECH's DC+Enterprise mix hit 21% of Q1FY27 revenue from 1% in FY26 on record INR13,100cr quarterly order intake anchored by a $1.1bn multi-year hyperscaler deal; FY27 EBITDA-margin guide raised 20%->23% and DC+Enterprise mix guide raised 30%->50% of revenue); REDINGTON/DCI/IVALUE on GPU/AI-infra distribution. Q1FY27 added two balance-sheet-scale entrants: HCLTECH is putting up to INR 3,500cr into its own AI-datacenter business with a 50MW long-term ambition ('megawatt isn't the product, it's the anchor'), and RELIANCE disclosed a 168 MW Meta data centre at Jamnagar built on its own balance sheet.
themes.driver: DC cooling LOIs converting (VENUSPIPES, AEROFLEX); hyperscaler/colo India capex (CUMMINSIND gensets, BLUESTARCO MEP); STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler optical-connectivity deal and 2.4x QoQ order-book jump to INR18,618cr; GPU/AI-infra orders.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Positions itself as one of India's leading manufacturers of heat exchangers and HVAC&R solutions for residential, commercial and industrial applications, with a diversified portfolio spanning Fin & Tube Coils, Bar & Plate, Complete HVAC Systems, Bus AC Systems, Refrigeration Components, Technical Tubes, Sheet Metal Parts and Tubings.
- Serves diverse end-use industries: HVAC, refrigeration, data centers, automotive, railways, industrial cooling, process applications, power and marine.
- Established international footprint across roughly 19 countries (UAE, USA, Italy, Canada, France, UK, Germany and others in Europe, plus Sri Lanka, Vietnam, Nepal, China, Brazil); CMD notes products reached customers in 14 countries during Q1 FY27.
- Export share of the revenue mix has risen steadily: 14.68% (FY24) to 15.69% (FY25) to 16.57% (FY26).

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Listing] Converted from a private to a public limited company and listed on NSE and BSE in October 2024.
- [Leadership] Founder-Chairman & Managing Director Mr. Santosh Kumar Yadav previously worked at Lloyd Electric & Engineering Limited before establishing KRN in 2017; holds a Diploma in Mechanical Engineering and a Diploma in Business Management (IMT Ghaziabad).
